items.editor_note: First outside coverage frames V4-Flash's affordability as the story, not Pro's flagship status.

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek's flagship V4 Pro entered late July already under scrutiny, benchmarked head-to-head against Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on cost, license, and serving price. Within days a rival low-cost model was already undercutting it on price-performance, and by July 31 DeepSeek's own retrained V4-Flash sibling was beating Pro on nine agent benchmarks.
editorial.whats_new: DeepSeek officially shipped V4-Flash on Jul 31, and outside coverage (The Information, Aug 2) is now framing the smaller, cheaper model as the standout — not flagship V4 Pro.
editorial.why_it_matters: Teams running DeepSeek for agent workloads should re-benchmark before assuming Pro is still the right default: V4-Flash now has both the better agent-benchmark story and growing outside coverage as the practical, affordable choice.
editorial.take_for_builders: Running DeepSeek V4 Pro for agent workloads? Re-benchmark against the now-shipped V4-Flash — outside coverage is already treating it as the practical default on cost.

status.detail: V4-Flash is officially released and outside coverage now frames it as DeepSeek's practical default over flagship V4 Pro.

open_questions: Does DeepSeek reposition V4-Flash as the default choice for agent workloads, or keep Pro as the flagship despite the benchmark loss?
Do independent evals confirm V4-Flash's nine-benchmark lead over Pro, or is this still DeepSeek's own reported result?
Does V4-Flash's pricing undercut V4 Pro enough to change the serving-cost calculus for teams already running Pro?
